title: How we fine-tuned a faster model for Patterns on Baseten
gist: Summarisation was most of the cost and half the latency of one product feature. The team distilled a month of a frontier model's production summaries into an adapter on a small open model. A coding agent ran the workflow, with a person approving each paid step.
changes: A workload owner replacing a frontier model with a small tuned one for a single job, using its own production outputs as the teacher. It is also an agent working on the model lever, not the engine.
caveats: Small evaluation, no head-to-head with the frontier teacher and no dollar figures. The authors say the untuned model mostly failed by running out of tokens; on answers it finished, both passed at the same rate. The base model had already been dropped from another provider's training list.

numbers.baseline: the same small open model untuned

bears_on.note: A narrow job moved from a frontier model to a small tuned one, trained on the frontier model's own outputs.
Most of the measured gain was fixing truncation, not better answers.
One company, one feature, its own traffic as training data.
